name: bash
description: Run a shell command with `bash -c` and wait for it to finish. Returns the exit code, stdout and stderr; long output is truncated keeping the head and tail. On timeout the command and all its children are killed. Each call starts a fresh shell, so `cd` and `export` do not persist: pass `cwd` and `env` instead. For servers, watchers or anything long-running, use `process_start`.

command.description: Shell command to run with `bash -c`. Pipes, redirects, `&&` and multi-line scripts are allowed.

cwd.description: Working directory for the command. Defaults to the sandbox working directory.

env.description: Extra environment variables for this command only.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the command and all its child processes after this many milliseconds. Defaults to 120000 (2 minutes).

exit_code.description: Exit status, or `null` if the command was killed by a signal.

signal.description: Signal number that terminated the command, if any.

stderr.description: Captured stderr (head and tail kept when truncated).

stdout.description: Captured stdout (head and tail kept when truncated).

timed_out.description: True if the command hit its timeout and was killed.

truncated.description: True if stdout or stderr was truncated.

name: file_read
description: Read a text file. Returns lines prefixed with their 1-based line numbers. Use `offset` and `limit` to page through large files. Binary files are detected and not returned; use `download` for those.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

offset.description: 1-based line number to start reading from. Defaults to 1.

path.description: Path of the file to read.

content.description: Requested lines, each formatted as `{line_number:>6}\t{line}` (like `cat -n`). Empty for binary files.

end_line.description: 1-based number of the last returned line (`start_line - 1` when nothing was returned).

is_binary.description: True if the file looks binary; `content` is then empty.

start_line.description: 1-based number of the first returned line.

total_lines.description: Total number of lines in the file.

truncated.description: True if the file has more lines after `end_line` or long lines were cut.

name: file_write
description: Create or overwrite a text file with the given content, creating parent directories as needed. Set `append` to add to the end instead. Prefer `file_edit` for changing part of an existing file.

append.description: Append `content` to the end of the file instead of replacing it.

path.description: Path of the file to write. Missing parent directories are created.

bytes_written.description: Number of bytes written by this call.

created.description: True if the file did not exist before.

name: file_edit
description: Replace an exact string in a file. `old_string` must match the file exactly, including whitespace and indentation, and must be unique unless `replace_all` is set; otherwise the edit fails and the file is unchanged. Read the file first. Returns a unified diff of the change.

old_string.description: Exact text to replace, including whitespace and indentation. Must occur exactly once unless `replace_all` is set.

path.description: Path of the file to edit.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence of `old_string` instead of requiring a unique match.

diff.description: Compact unified diff of the change.

name: file_delete
description: Delete a file, symlink or directory. Deleting a directory requires `recursive: true`.

path.description: Path of the file, symlink or directory to delete.

recursive.description: Required to delete a directory and everything inside it.

kind.description: Kind of entry that was deleted.

name: file_move
description: Move or rename a file or directory. Fails if the destination exists unless `overwrite` is set.

overwrite.description: Replace the destination if it already exists.

to.description: Destination path. Missing parent directories are created.

name: list_dir
description: List a directory's entries with their kind, size and permission bits. Increase `depth` to recurse. Skips .gitignore'd entries by default.

depth.description: How many directory levels to descend. 1 lists only direct children. Defaults to 1.

path.description: Directory to list. Defaults to the sandbox working directory.

respect_gitignore.description: Skip entries ignored by .gitignore and similar ignore files.

path.description: Path relative to the listed directory.

truncated.description: True if the entry limit was hit.

name: glob
description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern such as `**/*.rs` or `src/**/test_*.py`. Returns paths relative to `root`. Skips .gitignore'd files by default.

pattern.description: Glob pattern matched against paths relative to `root`, e.g. `**/*.rs` or `src/**/test_*.py`.

respect_gitignore.description: Skip files ignored by .gitignore and similar ignore files.

root.description: Directory to search from. Defaults to the sandbox working directory.

paths.description: Matching paths relative to the search root.

truncated.description: True if the result limit was hit.

name: grep
description: Search file contents for a regular expression (or a literal string with `literal: true`). Returns each matching line with its file path, line number and optional context lines. Skips .gitignore'd files; narrow the search with `root` and `glob`.

context_lines.description: Number of lines of context to include before and after each match. Defaults to 0.

glob.description: Only search files whose path matches this glob, e.g. `*.ts` or `src/**/*.py`.

literal.description: Treat `pattern` as a literal string instead of a regular expression.

pattern.description: Regular expression (Rust regex syntax) to search for, or a plain string when `literal` is set.

root.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the sandbox working directory.

matches.description: Matches grouped by file, in line order.

line.description: The matching line, without its trailing newline.

path.description: File path relative to the search root.

truncated.description: True if the match limit was hit.

name: process_start
description: Start a long-running command in the background (dev server, file watcher, REPL) and return immediately with a `process_id`. Read its output with `process_poll`, send input with `process_stdin`, stop it with `process_kill`.

command.description: Shell command to run in the background with `bash -c`.

cwd.description: Working directory for the process. Defaults to the sandbox working directory.

env.description: Extra environment variables for this process only.

pty.description: Run attached to a pseudo-terminal. Use for interactive programs (REPLs, prompts) that need a TTY.

pid.description: OS process ID inside the sandbox.

name: process_poll
description: Get a background process's status and the stdout/stderr it produced since the previous poll.

running.description: True while the process is still running.

signal.description: Terminating signal number, if killed by a signal.

stderr.description: Stderr produced since the previous poll.

stdout.description: Stdout produced since the previous poll (PTY output appears here).

truncated.description: True if output was dropped because the buffer overflowed between polls.

name: process_stdin
description: Write text to a background process's stdin. End with a newline to submit a line.

data.description: Text to write to the process's stdin. End with `\n` to submit a line.

name: process_kill
description: Stop a background process and all of its children.

signal.description: Signal sent to the whole process group: `TERM` (graceful, default), `INT` (like Ctrl-C) or `KILL` (immediate).

was_running.description: False if the process had already exited.

name: process_list
description: List the background processes started with `process_start`, both running and exited.

pid.description: OS process ID inside the sandbox.

pty.description: True if attached to a pseudo-terminal.

name: upload
description: Write a file from base64-encoded bytes, e.g. an image or archive. Use `file_write` for text.

content_base64.description: File content, base64-encoded (standard alphabet, padded). At most 10 MiB once decoded.

mode.description: Unix permission bits as a decimal number, e.g. 420 for 0644 or 493 for 0755. Defaults to 0644.

overwrite.description: Replace the file if it already exists.

path.description: Destination file path. Missing parent directories are created.

created.description: True if the file did not exist before.

name: download
description: Read a file as base64-encoded bytes, e.g. an image or archive. Use `file_read` for text.

max_bytes.description: Fail instead of returning files larger than this many bytes. Defaults to and is capped at 10485760 (10 MiB).

path.description: Path of the file to download.
